official.deadline_note: The deadline is the SNU graduate admission deadline itself - the GSFS is applied for at the same time as admission, so there is no separate scholarship deadline. The 2027 Spring round closed on 9 July 2026; the programme reopens every semester with the international graduate admission round, and the next call had not yet been published as of 10 October 2026.
official.application_cycle: 2027 Spring intake (Spring 2027 cycle); awarded every semester alongside SNU international graduate admissions
official.status_note: The latest published round - Call for GSFS Program of Spring 2027, posted 6 July 2026 on the SNU OGA scholarship notice board - closed at 5:00 PM KST on 9 July 2026, with admissions decisions after 5:00 PM on 20 November 2026 and GSFS results notified by e-mail in early December 2026. SNU publishes the application period as 'during the admission application period for international students every semester', so a new call is expected with the next international graduate admission round.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official wording: recipients 'will receive a full waiver of the admission fee and tuition fees for up to two academic years (four semesters)'. The OGA programme page states 'Full Tuition Fee' for '4 semesters maximum'. The KRW 90,000 application fee is explicitly NOT covered.
benefits: Full waiver of the admission fee and tuition fees for up to two academic years (four semesters)
Monthly stipend of at least KRW 500,000 - at least 1 year for Master's programme applicants and at least 2 years for Doctorate programme applicants
Additional OGA assistance: issuance of Certificate of Admission and Information Guide, and registration management
Award sustained by maintaining an average grade point of 3.0/4.3 and above (assessed at the end of each semester)
eligibility: Nationality: the applicant and both of their parents must not hold Korean nationality

Educational background: the entire formal education from primary school to the final degree required for the applied programme must have been completed outside Korea - applicants who have obtained a degree from a Korean university, including through a dual-degree programme, are NOT eligible (short-term exchange study in Korea is permitted)

Academic qualifications: Master's or Combined Master's & Doctoral applicants must hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and Doctoral applicants a master's degree or higher, from an accredited institution outside Korea
Programme selection: the applicant must apply to one of the designated colleges or schools participating in the GSFS Programme for that semester (the list changes every semester)
Admission to SNU: the applicant must apply and be successfully admitted to Seoul National University for that semester

SNU's programme page describes the target group as newly-admitted graduates from universities in East, Southeast and Central Asia, noting that students in China and Japan are not eligible; the Spring 2027 guide states that applicants holding nationality of countries not classified as Advanced Economies by the IMF are given priority consideration

Apply to a designated college or school participating in the GSFS Programme for the relevant semester
Maintain an average grade point of 3.0/4.3 or above, assessed at the end of each semester, to sustain the scholarship
documents: Online application for admission to SNU with the 'Application for Scholarship' box checked (scholarship applied for at the same time)

Admission documents submitted to the relevant SNU college or school - selection is made from the admission documents, including transcripts and grades, the proposed study plan and the personal statement
Degree certificate(s) from the final degree completed outside Korea supporting eligibility (Master's applicants: bachelor's or higher; Doctoral applicants: master's or higher)
selection_criteria: The applicant's overall academic trajectory and potential
Performance in previous studies, as evidenced by transcripts and grades
The quality and feasibility of the proposed study plan
The depth and sincerity of the personal statement
Any additional achievements or qualifications relevant to the chosen field of study
Evaluation and selection are conducted independently by each graduate school/college at SNU

Monthly stipend of at least KRW 500,000 for 1 year (Master's) or 2 years (Doctorate)

official.application_route: Apply online through SNU's Office of Admissions graduate application portal during the international admission period and tick 'Application for Scholarship' - the scholarship has no separate application or deadline
official.citizenship_residency: The applicant and both of their parents must not hold Korean nationality; there is no residency requirement
official.international_eligibility: Yes - by design for foreign (non-Korean) students only; applicants holding Korean nationality, or whose parents hold Korean nationality, are not eligible
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applicants must apply to one of the designated colleges or schools participating in the GSFS Programme for that semester; the participating list and spot allocations are published in the semester guide from the SNU Office of Global Affairs and change every semester (Spring 2027: 22 openings across 15 designated colleges/graduate schools)
official.research_requirement: A proposed study plan forms part of the admission documents reviewed by each graduate school and is assessed for quality and feasibility; no separate research proposal is published as a scholarship requirement
official.duration: Full tuition (and admission fee) waiver for up to 2 academic years (four semesters); monthly stipend of at least KRW 500,000 for 1 year (Master's) or 2 years (Doctorate), with amount and duration varying by college/school
official.description: The Graduate Scholarship for Excellent Foreign Students (GSFS) is Seoul National University's scholarship for newly admitted international graduate students (Master's or PhD), providing a full waiver of admission and tuition fees for up to four semesters together with a monthly living stipend of at least KRW 500,000. Around 20 recipients are selected each semester - 22 for the 2027 Spring intake - by the designated colleges and schools from the admission documents. The scholarship application is submitted simultaneously with the online application for admission to SNU during the international student admission period each semester.
official.program_type: University-funded graduate scholarship for international students (Master's and PhD)

applicant_utility.summary: SNU's GSFS gives newly admitted foreign graduate students full tuition plus at least KRW 500,000 a month, but you can only be considered by applying through SNU's regular online admission form with the scholarship box ticked - there is no separate scholarship application or deadline. Roughly 20-22 places a semester are spread across about fifteen designated colleges, and each college picks its own winners straight from the admission file. The hard gate is your background: every stage of your schooling must have been completed outside Korea and neither parent may hold Korean nationality, so any Korean-awarded degree anywhere in your history is disqualifying. Winning is only half the job - you must hold a 3.0/4.3 average every semester to keep the money.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong Master's or PhD applicants from outside Korea - especially from countries not classified as IMF advanced economies - targeting one of the designated SNU colleges and able to front the KRW 90,000 application fee.
application_readiness_checklist: Download the current semester's GSFS guide from the SNU OGA scholarship notice board and confirm your target college/school is on the designated list with an open spot that semester
Verify that neither you nor either parent holds Korean nationality and that no degree - including a dual degree - was awarded by a Korean institution
Draft the study plan and personal statement early: they are formally assessed for quality, feasibility and sincerity, and there is no separate scholarship essay to compensate for a weak one
Have certified degree certificates and full transcripts ready to upload with the admission application
Budget for the KRW 90,000 application fee - it is explicitly not covered and there are no waivers
Plan your first-year grade target around the 3.0/4.3 sustainability threshold before you enrol
common_rejection_risks: Any Korean-awarded degree in your history (including via a dual-degree programme) makes you ineligible regardless of your grades
Applying to a college or school that is not on the designated GSFS list for that particular semester
Forgetting to tick 'Application for Scholarship' inside the admission form - miss it and your file is never reviewed for GSFS
Assuming a separate scholarship deadline exists and missing the admission deadline instead
Letting the semester average drop below 3.0/4.3 after selection and losing renewal
Applying in a round where your preferred college has no allocated spot (spots per college can be as low as one)
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The KRW 90,000 application fee is explicitly not covered. Airfare, settlement and installation costs, National Health Insurance premiums, Korean language training and any living costs above the monthly stipend are not published as covered by GSFS.
document_audit: The 'Application for Scholarship' checkbox lives inside the admission form itself - if it is unchecked, no scholarship review happens at all
Transcripts and grades are the core selection evidence; there is no separate scholarship dossier or recommendation portal for GSFS
The proposed study plan is judged on feasibility, not just ambition - a vague plan weakens the admission file that decides the scholarship
Only final recipients are notified by e-mail; silence after the decision date means not selected, so do not wait on a rejection letter
After admission, stipend administration runs through the individual college/school's scholarship staff, not OGA - expect contact from your department
alerts: The most recent round (2027 Spring) closed on 9 July 2026; the next call is expected alongside the next international graduate admission round but had not been published as of 10 October 2026 - check the OGA scholarship notice board monthly
There is no standalone GSFS portal or deadline: your scholarship depends entirely on submitting the admission application in time with the scholarship box ticked
Recipients are in principle restricted from taking leave of absence; if unavoidable, you must contact OGA and your college/school in advance
The stipend amount and its duration vary by college/school because departments co-fund the living support - confirm the exact terms with your college after receiving an offer
The eligible-country/participating-college lists change every semester, so last semester's list is not reliable
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One submission only: complete SNU's online graduate admission application during the international admission window, tick 'Application for Scholarship', pay the KRW 90,000 fee; the designated colleges/schools then select from the admission documents and notify only the final recipients individually by e-mail.
